market_specific_notes: The single biggest cost and timing variable is not the city, it is your vaccination records. USCIS lists exactly which ones it means, and arriving without them means either repeat doses or blood work to prove immunity.

USCIS warns that “Many health insurance plans do not cover all portions of this examination.” Bring the card, but ask the office whether it accepts the plan for immigration medical examinations specifically before you assume anything.

Under the USCIS blanket designation, all state and local health departments are recognised as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment. In San Francisco that points at the San Francisco Department of Public Health — for that category, and for vaccinations rather than the whole examination.
Most of the checklist below can be settled in a single phone call before you book. Doing it in that order is what stops a second visit from becoming a surprise.
local_vetting_points: Start at uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon and search your own ZIP, then widen the radius deliberately rather than accepting the first list.
Check the office appears in that federal list under the name on its door and on its invoices.
Ask whether laboratory work is sent out or run in-house, because that decides whether the form is ready the same week.
Ask what the office does when a vaccination record is incomplete, before you find out on the day.
Confirm who signs the form and when, not just who performs the examination.
typical_cost_ranges: There is no published price. USCIS says: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.”

USCIS's own guidance is to ring around: “It may be helpful to call a few civil surgeons to find out how much they charge for the immigration medical examination. The cost of an immigration medical examination can vary significantly.”

Ask every office to break the number into examination, tuberculosis and syphilis testing, missing vaccines, form completion and any follow-up visit. A cheaper headline with vaccines excluded is not cheaper.
Filing Form I-693 with USCIS costs $0. The filing fee that carries real money is the I-485: paper $1,440 or online $1,390 for an applicant over 14.
payment_options: USCIS tells applicants to check acceptable forms of payment with the office in advance. Do that on the same call as the price question.
Ask whether any part of the fee is due at booking, and what happens to it if a second visit is needed.
wait_time_notes: Appointment availability and form completion are different questions. An office can see you on Tuesday and still not have a signed form for two weeks.
A positive tuberculosis test triggers a chest X-ray. Ask what that does to both the price and the timeline before it happens.
availability_notes: Ask whether a quoted turnaround assumes complete vaccination records, because most quoted turnarounds do.
If a filing deadline is close, say the date out loud on the phone and ask the office to confirm it can meet it.
named_resources_or_providers: USCIS Find a Civil Surgeon locator (official) — uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon
San Francisco Department of Public Health — sf.gov/departments/department-public-health. USCIS recognises local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment.
USCIS Form I-693 page — uscis.gov/i-693, for the current form edition and filing instructions.
Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: San Francisco is a small city inside a large civil surgeon market. A ZIP search on the official USCIS locator will return a short list; widening it a few miles will return a much longer one. Decide first how far you are willing to travel twice, because a second visit is common.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Search the official USCIS locator by ZIP, then widen the radius on purpose.
Ask for the price broken into examination, labs, vaccines, form completion and follow-up.
Ask whether labs are in-house or sent out, since that sets the real turnaround.
Gather the vaccination records USCIS names before the first visit.
Tell the office whether the I-485 is going by mail or online.
Confirm the form edition and the intended signing date.

heading: Booking a San Francisco civil surgeon: plan for two visits, not one
i693_document_requirements: The current edition of Form I-693. Ask the office which edition it uses before the visit.
Government-issued photo identification, such as a valid passport or driver's licence.
For an applicant aged 14 or younger, USCIS accepts identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name — a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

A record of your vaccinations or immunisations. USCIS names them: DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Your health insurance card, and payment in a form the office accepts.
vaccination_handling_notes: Chase the records before you book, not between visits. It is the one part of the process entirely within your control.
California residents can request their own immunisation record through the state registry; ask the clinic which record format it will accept before you pay for anything.
For refugees adjusting status, the vaccination assessment may be completed at a state or local health department under the USCIS blanket designation.
bilingual_support: The federal locator carries a Languages Spoken filter listing well over a hundred named languages. It is the office's own declaration to USCIS, which is a stronger signal than a website banner.
Filtering finds a language in the practice. It does not guarantee the person walking you through the form speaks it — ask which part of the visit is covered.
appointment_booking_notes: Settle the mail-or-online question before the exam. Filing I-485 by mail, the envelope stays sealed. Filing online, USCIS instructs you to open it, upload the form, and keep the original and envelope until the case is decided.
Confirm the form edition and the signing date. Only the 01/20/25 edition is accepted for forms signed on or after 3 July 2025.
Ask whether the slot you are given is intake, examination, or the whole path to a signed form.

Before you pay, ask when the sealed packet is released and who to contact for a correction if something on the form is wrong. The answer to the second question tells you more about the office than the answer to the first.
